summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, and recent ventral hernia repair was admitted for severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and syncope. He presented with tachycardia and volume depletion, was unable to tolerate oral intake, and had a history of presyncopal episodes linked to abdominal pain. Imaging showed no acute surgical or pulmonary process, but revealed a 1.7 cm right hilar lymph node of uncertain significance. The abdominal pain was attributed to acute on chronic pancreatitis. He was managed with IV fluids, pain control, and gradual diet advancement. His tachycardia resolved with rehydration and pain control. He was discharged home after tolerating a regular diet and achieving stable pain control, with follow-up planned for the lymph node and continuation of home medications including Creon and metformin.
